title: Identifiability of Student Data in Transit
description: Student ID, course, and submission timestamp in the data flow could be used to identify the specific student and their academic activities to unauthorized observers intercepting the transmission.

title: Disclosure of Assignment Content During Transmission
description: The work file submitted by the student contains potentially sensitive academic work that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the data flow is intercepted or not properly encrypted.

title: Student Identity Usurpation at Source
description: The student's login credentials could be compromised, allowing an attacker to impersonate the student and submit assignments on their behalf.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Student Submissions
description: The Grades Portal Web App may store student submissions and personal data in a way that allows unauthorized access or improper disclosure to third parties.

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Submission
description: Without proper audit trails and cryptographic signatures, the student could potentially deny submitting an assignment, or the system could not prove the student's identity at the time of submission.

title: Student Identification via Data in Transit
description: Student ID, course, and file reference transmitted in the data flow can directly identify the student and their specific academic submissions, creating identification risk during transmission.

title: Linkability of Student Submissions
description: Metadata including student ID, course, and file reference can be used to link the student's submissions and grades across different contexts or systems, potentially enabling profiling.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure at Destination
description: Assignment & Grading Service may disclose student identification and submission data to unauthorized parties or systems without proper access controls.

title: Data Usage Beyond Intended Purpose
description: Assignment & Grading Service may use student identification and submission data for purposes beyond grading, such as analytics, profiling, or third-party sharing.

title: Linkability of submission meta-data in the review queue
description: The data flow could reveal meta-data about which students are submitting work, potentially allowing linking of submissions to specific students through the review queue.

title: Identification of teacher's course assignments
description: The teacher's request for submissions reveals which courses they teach and which students are enrolled, potentially exposing teacher-student relationships.

title: Over-disclosure of student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App may display more information about submissions than necessary for the teacher's review, potentially exposing sensitive student data.

title: Unauthorized access to submission queue
description: If the teacher's authentication is compromised, unauthorized parties could impersonate the teacher and access the submission queue.

title: Student Identification via Submission Data
description: Student names and work content transmitted in the data flow can be used to identify individual students, potentially exposing their identity to unauthorized parties if the flow is intercepted.

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Submissions
description: The teacher (destination) receives student names, work content, and submission times, which could be accessed by unauthorized individuals if teacher credentials are compromised or if access controls are insufficient.

title: Unintended Use of Student Work
description: The teacher may use student submission data for purposes beyond grading, such as sharing with third parties, using in publications, or for other educational/administrative purposes without explicit consent.

title: Excessive Data Sharing
description: The portal shares student names, full work content, and submission times with the teacher, potentially sharing more data than necessary for the grading function, violating data minimization principles.

title: Data Interception in Transit
description: Grades and feedback data transmitted between Teacher and Grades Portal could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly encrypted, exposing sensitive student performance information.

title: Linkability of Student Records
description: The student id included in the data flow could be used to link this grade/feedback record to other student records, potentially creating a comprehensive profile of the student's academic performance across multiple systems.

title: Excessive Data Sharing by Teacher
description: The teacher shares grader id along with grade and feedback, which may be more data than necessary for the immediate purpose of recording a grade, potentially exposing teacher identity unnecessarily.

title: Student Identification from Stored Data
description: The Grades Portal Web App stores student id with grades and feedback, enabling identification of students from the stored data, which could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems.

title: Lack of Audit Trail for Grade Recording
description: Without proper logging and audit mechanisms, the teacher could deny having recorded a particular grade or feedback, making it difficult to resolve disputes or verify grading integrity.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: The grade records database may be accessible to unauthorized personnel, potentially exposing sensitive student grades, feedback, and personal identifiers.

title: Inadequate Access Controls on Database
description: The database may lack proper access controls, allowing unauthorized users to view, modify, or delete grade records.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Grade records transmitted between the grading service and database could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit.

title: Student Identification Through Grade Records
description: Student IDs in grade records could be used to identify students and link their academic performance to their identities.

title: Lack of Audit Trail for Grading Actions
description: Without proper logging, grading actions could be denied or disputed, making it difficult to establish accountability.

title: Inadequate Data Retention Policies
description: Grade records may be retained longer than necessary, increasing the risk of unauthorized access and potential misuse of historical data.

title: Student Identity Disclosure During Grade Request
description: When the student requests their grades, they must provide identifying information (e.g., student ID, username) to the system. This act of sharing their identity with the Grades Portal Web App creates a risk that their personal identity could be exposed or misused.

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Grades
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives and processes student grade data. If access controls are inadequate, unauthorized parties (e.g., other students, malicious actors) could access the student's grades and feedback, leading to privacy violations.

title: Grade Data Tampering
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) stores and processes grade data. Without proper integrity controls, there is a risk that grades or feedback could be altered, deleted, or manipulated by unauthorized users or system vulnerabilities.

title: Linkability of Grade Data to Student Identity
description: Data in transit (DF8) contains student grades and feedback that could be linked to the student's identity through metadata (e.g., timestamps, IP addresses, request patterns). This could enable correlation attacks that reveal the student's identity or link grades to other personal information.

title: Linkability of Parent-Child Account Relationship
description: Metadata about the parent-child account linkage in the data flow could be used to link the parent to the child, potentially revealing the child's identity to unauthorized observers monitoring the data flow.

title: Identification of Child Through Grades Data
description: The grades data processed and stored by the Grades Portal Web App could be used to identify the child, especially if combined with other information or if the grades are accessible to unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grades
description: The Grades Portal Web App may store or process grades in a way that exposes them to unauthorized parties, violating the expectation of confidentiality for sensitive academic information.

title: Parent Account Impersonation
description: If the parent's authentication mechanism is weak, an attacker could impersonate the parent and access the child's grades, leading to unauthorized data access.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history transmitted between the portal and parent could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially exposing sensitive educational information.

title: Unauthorized Parent Access via Impersonation
description: The portal may allow an unauthorized individual to impersonate a parent and access a child's grades and submission history if authentication mechanisms are insufficient.

title: Parent Account Compromise Leading to Data Disclosure
description: If the parent's account credentials are compromised, unauthorized parties could access the child's sensitive educational data including grades and feedback.

title: Child Identification Through Grade Data
description: The portal may inadvertently reveal which child's grades are being displayed, potentially allowing identification of the child even when the parent is the intended recipient.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transmitted over network to third-party cloud provider, creating risk of interception or eavesdropping by unauthorized parties during transit.

title: Data Exposure in Transit
description: Sensitive student data including grades and account directory information is exposed during transmission, potentially allowing unauthorized access to personal and academic information.

title: Unauthorized Access at Destination
description: Cloud hosting provider may have inadequate security controls, creating risk of unauthorized access to stored grade records, assignments, and account directory data.

title: Identification from Stored Data
description: Account directory and grade records stored at cloud provider can be used to identify students and link their academic information to their identities.

title: Inappropriate Data Sharing
description: Assignment & Grading Service shares full grade records and account directory with third-party provider, potentially exceeding necessary data minimization principles.

title: Inappropriate disclosure of grade information
description: The grading service may create student, parent, or teacher views that disclose grade information beyond what is authorized or necessary, potentially exposing sensitive academic data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly implemented or enforced

title: Identification through grade records
description: Grade records shared with the grading service could be used to identify specific students, potentially exposing their academic information and creating a privacy risk.
assumptions: Grade records contain identifying information such as student IDs or names

title: Data linkage through grade records
description: Grade records transmitted between the database and grading service could be linked with other data sources to identify individuals or create detailed profiles.
assumptions: Grade records can be correlated with other data held by the grading service
